scope: Independent read-only review of optimized tick/Unicorn memory-hook divergence, C aliasing/alignment/volatile/sparse ABI concerns, and emitted O2 list-insertion contract.

o2_replica.qualification: reconstructed diagnostic replica; not retained authenticated firmware object

bounded_stock_comparison.scope: one valid two-expiry case; no source memory-hook invariants

hook_range_matrix.observation: unused address range succeeds; a range covering accessed RAM reproduces the missing unconditional load

observations: I reran the standalone 32-case machine reproduction under Unicorn 2.1.4. It uses three unchanged optimized machine-code bodies totaling 296 bytes, synthetic aligned RAM, and an empty memory-hook callback.

One due task completes under every tested memory-hook mode. Two due tasks complete with no memory hook or a code hook only; READ, WRITE, and combined memory hooks each fault at 0x10296, with or without the code hook.

On the second list insertion, the code trace proceeds from 0x10292 to 0x10296 without visiting 0x10290. Disassembly shows 0x10290 is unconditional encoding 0x6842 (LDR r2,[r0,#4]). The corresponding ready-list pxIndex cell at 0x2006a4dc still holds 0x2006a4e0, but r2 is zero at the fault.

The empty callback rules out project callback logic as a necessary cause; code-hook-only reads of R2/XPSR do not reproduce the fault. The hook-range matrix reports success for an unused address range and failure when hooked range covers accessed RAM. This supports a bounded memory-hook-sensitive Unicorn execution diagnosis but does not establish the emulator internal root cause.

A separate one-input comparison reports stock final-state equality and independent graph-model pass for O2, O2-noalias, and O0 with source memory hooks omitted. It is observational diagnostic evidence only; source memory invariants are absent and it receives no passing coverage credit.

source_review.alignment_and_sparse_abi: No concrete misalignment or field-width defect identified in the reviewed 32-bit List_t/ListItem_t compatibility layouts or O2 insertion accesses; ABI assertions cover structure size and accessed TCB offsets, not a complete recovered TCB.
source_review.volatile: Recovered global kernel cells use volatile lvalues where required; list/TCB object fields are ordinary accesses under the kernel critical/scheduler preconditions.
source_review.aliasing_caveat: Pinned FreeRTOS deliberately casts the MiniListItem sentinel address to ListItem_t* and accesses the shared prefix through ListItem_t; potential effective-type/strict-aliasing concern under ISO C. Original G2 compiler flags are unknown. Same memory-hook failure occurs in the no-strict-aliasing diagnostic, so aliasing is not established as cause.
source_review.o2_contract: At vListInsertEnd, 0x10290 is unconditional encoding 0x6842 (LDR r2,[r0,#4]); following 0x10292 loads the item count and 0x10296 dereferences r2. For the failing second insertion, 0x10290 is skipped in the Unicorn trace even though pxIndex remains valid. This is a machine-execution observation, not evidence of an invalid source pointer or hardware behavior.

disposition: The specific memory-hooked O2 failure is reproduced as a bounded Unicorn execution limitation, with its exact internal root cause unresolved. Keep the full O2 validation gate blocked: its unchanged verifier still exits 1 and no optimized PASS exists. The one-case no-memory-hook stock/model agreement receives no coverage credit; the O0 full 271-case result is separate.
